title: Excavator chained on a lowboy (rear view)
blurb: Heavy equipment from behind. The rear view is where lights, plate, and overhang get judged; chains read as presence hints, never as counted tie-downs.
photo_credit: Development photo, openly licensed (see repo docs). Inputs: bed 48 ft, load 25 ft.

calibration.axis: x (front at bed_min_x, rear at bed_max_x)
calibration.method: pixels-per-inch = trailer_bed mask bitmap tight extent along x (3124 px) / user-supplied bed length (48.0 ft = 576 in)

measurements.name: rear_overhang
measurements.method: rearmost cargo extent (mask bitmap tight edge, else bbox) minus the bed rear edge, scaled by the calibration; rear = image-right end of the bed extent

measurements.name: load_centroid_vs_axle

value.direction: ahead of the axle (toward the front)

measurements.method: bitmap-weighted centroid of all cargo masks along the bed axis vs the axle estimate position (midpoint of axle centres when several), scaled by the calibration; positive offset = centroid behind the axle
measurements.confidence_basis: cargo det-0011-feabb4 conf 0.61; axle_estimate axle-0015-07650f conf 0.95; axle_estimate axle-0016-b85e01 conf 0.92

uncertainty.basis: one bitmap-weighted standard deviation of the cargo pixels along the bed axis (the load's own spread), floored at 2 in; a photo shows where the bulk sits, not how heavy it is

measurements.name: tarp_coverage
measurements.method: tarp/canvas mask area overlapping the cargo area, as a percentage of the cargo area (bitmap union on the image canvas)
measurements.reason: load type is 'excavator', not loose material; the tarp check only applies to loose loads

measurements.name: tiedown_coverage_gaps
measurements.method: tie-down anchor positions mapped onto the bed axis (anchor centre x in bed coordinates); spans between neighbouring anchors and the bed ends, scaled by the calibration
measurements.reason: no tie-down detections in this detection set: tie-downs are counted from anchor close-up photos plus tap-to-correct, and close-up coordinates live in the close-up photo's own image space, so they cannot be placed on this photo's bed axis

notes: load_centroid_vs_axle is a visual estimate of where the load's bulk sits; it is not a weight measurement

verdicts.finding: The load's front edge sits 0.0 in from the front of the bed, inside the 6 in blocking threshold: it has no real room to slide forward under braking.
verdicts.confidence_basis: front gap derived deterministically from the Day 2 calibration (bed front edge, pixels-per-inch) and the frontmost cargo extent (cargo det-0011-feabb4); geometry shows slide room, it cannot prove what the load rests against

verdicts.finding: This load needs 4 tie-down(s) for its length (25 ft), but no tie-downs could be counted: tie-downs are counted from anchor close-up photos plus any you mark by tapping them on the photo, and neither was supplied. Full-frame photos cannot count straps reliably (they are too thin to read at that distance).
verdicts.confidence_basis: no close-up detection set and no user tie-down marks supplied

verdicts.finding: This is a heavy wheeled/tracked load, but its weight was not supplied, and 393.130's requirements trigger at 10,000 lb: at or above that weight the machine needs at least 4 tie-downs. Supply the machine's weight to decide this check. Whether buckets, booms and other accessories are lowered and secured separately cannot be verified from a photo.
verdicts.confidence_basis: missing input: weight_lb (the 10,000 lb trigger cannot be evaluated)

verdicts.cfr_citation: 49 CFR Part 393, Subpart I (overhang; lights and plate visibility)
verdicts.finding: Overhang: the load extends 48.5 in past the rear of the bed. Lights and plate: the rear photo read reports the tail lights and license plate obscured by the load.
verdicts.minimum_fix: Shorten or reposition the load to remove the overhang; any load still extending well past the rear (over 4 ft) needs a red flag by day and lights at night at its extreme end, and the load itself still has to be fully secured; Reposition the load (or fit auxiliary lights / relocate the plate) so the tail lights and license plate are fully visible from behind
verdicts.confidence_basis: rear_overhang measurement: cargo det-0011-feabb4 conf 0.61; lights/plate from the dual-model cross-check rear read (Muse Spark); SAM has no equivalent signal
verdicts.citation: 49 CFR Part 393, Subpart I (overhang; lights and plate visibility)
verdicts.fix: Shorten or reposition the load to remove the overhang; any load still extending well past the rear (over 4 ft) needs a red flag by day and lights at night at its extreme end, and the load itself still has to be fully secured; Reposition the load (or fit auxiliary lights / relocate the plate) so the tail lights and license plate are fully visible from behind

verdicts.cfr_citation: 49 CFR 393.100 (load placement; visual estimate only here)
verdicts.finding: Weight placement cannot be called from this photo: the photo estimate puts the bulk at 41% of the bed length and the bulk sits 189.4 in ahead of the axle (+/-168.3 in), the direction you want, so placement cannot be decided from this photo. A photo shows where the bulk sits, not how heavy it is.
verdicts.confidence_basis: cargo det-0011-feabb4 conf 0.61; axle_estimate axle-0015-07650f conf 0.95; axle_estimate axle-0016-b85e01 conf 0.92; visual estimate only, never a PASS
verdicts.citation: 49 CFR 393.100 (load placement; visual estimate only here)

verdicts.finding: Edge protection cannot be judged from the evidence supplied: it needs a close-up of each strap where it crosses an edge, read for protectors. Take an anchor close-up per tie-down and run the cross-check.
verdicts.confidence_basis: no close-up cross-check evidence about straps over edges

verdicts.finding: Tie-down strength cannot be checked from the photo: a photo cannot verify working load limit ratings or load weight, and this check needs both numbers. Missing: no tie-down working load limit ratings were supplied; no load weight was supplied. Supply the load weight and each tie-down's rating and this check runs on those numbers.
verdicts.confidence_basis: not computable: no tie-down working load limit ratings were supplied; no load weight was supplied

report.headline: Excavator overhang blocks lights needs immediate fix
report.body:
Fix the overhang. The load sticks out 48.5 inches past the rear. The tail lights and license plate are obscured. Shorten or reposition to remove it. If still over 4 feet, add a red flag by day and lights at night on the end.
Forward blocking passes. The front sits 0.0 inches from the front, inside the 6 inch limit.
Tie-down count could not be told. This 25 foot load needs 4 tie-downs. Add anchor close-up photos or tap tie-downs on the photo. Heavy equipment securement could not be told. Supply machine weight, since at or above 10,000 pounds needs 4 tie-downs. Weight placement could not be told from this photo. Supply weight details, since a photo only shows bulk position. Edge protection could not be told. Supply a close-up of each strap at each edge. Tie-down strength could not be told. Supply tie-down ratings and load weight. A photo cannot verify strap tension, tie-down ratings, or load weight.
